newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stock index rises to close above 2,100.
newsitem.headline: French stock index rises to close above 2,100.

text.p: French stocks rallied more than one percent on Wednesday, propelling the blue-chip CAC-40 index above the 2,100 level, on investor relief that the Federal Reserve did not raise U.S. interest rates.
Brokers said the bourse hitched itself to the rising bond markets after having trailed other markets for months.
"The environment is very favourable after the Fed decision. As the bourse felt like climbing, it took this as a pretext," a trader said.
The CAC-40 index finished up 21.91 points, or 1.05 percent, at 2,103.41, while the CAC-40 September futures contract rose 14 points to 2,100.
Volume was a heavy 6.3 billion francs.
First-half results generated a lot of activity in individual stocks.

Shares in luxury goods group LVMH fell against the trend, closing down 2.82 percent at 1,101 francs, on nervousness ahead of the group's results due on Thursday morning. Its first half sales grew very slowly and currency trends are still negative.

Insurer Axa's shares jumped 3.85 percent to 297 francs after the company reported a jump in net attributable profit to 1.98 billion francs from 1.30 billion for the first half. "The results were significantly better than expected," a trader said.
"Axa is the best insurance stock in the market," said another trader.
Promodes shares rose 3.86 percent to 1,372 francs as investors applauded the retailer's move to acquire control of Italy's hyper and supermarkets concern Gruppo G.
"The market is reacting positively to this news -- to any news of expansion abroad -- because French retailers can only expand now if they expand abroad," one trader said.
Shares in carmaker Renault closed up 3.95 percent at 123.80 francs after the group announced it would cut prices in France by up to five percent on some models to recapture lost market share.
